display.title: The Days of Awe: Crowning Hashem as Our King
display.summary_short: Why the Ten Days of Teshuvah are called the Days of Awe, what kind of 'fear' they mean, and how the shofar moves Hashem from the Throne of Judgment to the Throne of Mercy.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given just before Rosh Hashanah. Uncle Yossi explains that the Yomim Noraim, the Ten Days of Teshuvah from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, are 'days of awe' because Hashem decides our health, food, clothing, shelter and life itself for the coming year. He distinguishes between two kinds of fear: fear of punishment, and the higher fear of doing anything against the will of Hashem, our Commander-in-Chief. During these days we resolve to stop doing wrong and do only mitzvos, returning to Hashem through teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah, davening more carefully and giving more charity. When we call out 'Avinu Malkeinu' and crown Hashem as our Father and King, He accepts the coronation, and, as our Sages teach, at the sound of the shofar He rises from the Throne of Judgment to the Throne of Mercy. He ends by urging children to find out when shofar is blown in their shul and to tell their friends.
display.lesson: The Days of Awe call us to be careful not to go against Hashem's will, and to crown Him as King through teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.
